item.title: Ukraine officials to boycott Paralympics for letting Russians compete under their flag
item.description: Ukraine said Wednesday that its officials will not attend the Winter Paralympics next month over organizers’ decision to allow a handful of Russian and Belarusian athletes to compete under their flags

item.title: Olympians Hilary Knight and Brittany Bowe engaged at Milan Cortina Games
item.description: Speedskater Brittany Bowe may not have medaled, but she is leaving the Winter Olympics with at least one piece of hardware after longtime girlfriend Hilary Knight proposed at the Winter Olympics

item.title: From the sports desk: Three overtimes, three thrilling men’s hockey finishes
item.description: Hello from Milan and Cortina, where we’re heading toward the homestretch of these Winter Games.

item.title: Mikaela Shiffrin storms to gold in the slalom, ending an eight-year medal drought
item.description: American skier Mikaela Shiffrin sits in first place in the slalom at the Milan Cortina Winter Olympics after the first of two runs Wednesday.

item.title: After hitting bottom twice following Olympic glory, Nick Goepper finds joy once again
item.description: U.S. skiier Nick Goepper suffered depression after winning Olympic medals. He says changes in his life has ensured it won't happen again.

item.title: Figure skater Alysa Liu looks to break medal drought for women of Team USA
item.description: An American woman has not medaled in women’s singles at the Olympics in twenty years. Alysa Liu is well-positioned to change that, entering the free skate in third place. Liu retired after the Beijing Olympics at just 16, but came back and says she has rediscovered the joy of skating. NBC News’ Stephanie Gosk reports.

item.title: Ex-South Korean president found guilty of insurrection over martial law order
item.description: Yoon Suk Yeol, the impeached president of South Korea, was found guilty of insurrection and sentenced to life in prison on Thursday over his failed attempt to impose martial law on the U.S. ally

item.title: U.S. military pushes more weaponry into the Middle East for possible strikes on Iran
item.description: WASHINGTON — The Defense Department is sending a large array of additional weaponry to the Middle East, including more warships, air defenses and submarines, in preparation for a possible military strike on Iran if President Donald Trump makes that decision, according to U.S. officials and information from public tracking.
